thread:
Micah: Heads-up — after the kv-layout tweak merged yesterday, we're seeing a latency bump on GQA path for seqlen ~6k. p95 up ~18% on the nightly canary. :thinking_face:
Elaine: ugh. which change specifically? the block packing switch?
Micah: the commit was `kvpack: prefer compact blocks when fragmentation > 0.6` (clifford's PR). I ran a quick local run: p50 stable but p95/p99 increased.
Raj: do you have perf profiles? flamegraphs or hotspot CPU traces would help.
Micah: perf-bot posted the canary trace: https://perf.internal/canary/ci/4872 — looks like attention kernel fallback happening more often.
perf-bot: Canary 4872 summary: 6k seq, batch=1, model=gqa-mqa-v2 -> p50 120ms, p95 310ms (baseline p95 262ms). Kernel switch count up 3.6x.
Sam: that sounds like KV-cache fragmentation causing page miss + fallback to non-paged attn kernel. Does the autotuner change thresholds for blocksize rounding?
Elaine: yep, the new packing reduces number of pages but increases contiguous block split when per-slice sizes vary. If blocks cross a page boundary, we fall back to the slow kernel.
Raj: can we repro with the microbench? try `bench_attn --model gqa-mqa-v2 --seqlen 6144 --batch 1 --kv-layout=packed` and `--kv-layout=legacy` and compare kernel names in logs.
Micah: repro steps I used: ```
# run on devbox
./bench_attn --model gqa-mqa-v2 --seqlen 6144 --batch 1 --runs 50 --dump-kernels > kernels.txt
grep -E "kernel=pagkv|kernel=paged_attn|kernel=kernel_fallback" kernels.txt | sort | uniq -c
```
Sam: what do the counts look like?
Micah: with packed layout: `kernel=paged_attn 18`, `kernel_fallback 32`. legacy: `kernel=paged_attn 44`, `kernel_fallback 6`.
Elaine: that matches hypothesis — packed layout increases misaligned block splits. We tuned packing for memory, not alignment.
Raj: possible mitigations: 1) change packing to respect page-aligned block boundaries for multi-query (MQA) lanes, 2) adjust autotuner seqlen cutoff so >4096 uses alternate kernel path, 3) patch kernel to handle split blocks (expensive).
Sam: patching kernel is risky. Quick experiment: try a soft rollback of the pack threshold to previous value and run CI canary. Or add a small heuristic: if fragmentation > X and seqlen > Y, force legacy layout.
Micah: I pushed a branch `kvpack/heuristic-rollback` with the old threshold and an override flag `--kvpack-backcompat`. Ran microbench: p95 went back to 268ms, fallback count down to 8.
Elaine: nice. Can we add a unit test that exercises a high-variance per-head slice distribution so we don't regress again? Also add a telemetry counter for `kvpack.misaligned_splits` so we can alert.
Raj: agree on telemetry. I'll file a small follow-up to add a seqlen-based autotuner rule: `if seqlen >= 4096 and mqa_enabled -> prefer legacy alignment`. Keep it gated behind lab flags.
Sam: next steps: Micah to run full canary with heuristic-rollback (owner), Raj to add telemetry + autotuner rule, Elaine to add unit test, I'll coordinate deploy. ETA tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
Micah: starting the canary run now — will paste links and p95 numbers when done. :eyes:
perf-bot: canary run queued #4880. status: running.
Micah: (later) canary 4880 finished: p95 270ms, kernel_fallback count 9, `kvpack.misaligned_splits` 146. Rolling the heuristic-rollback to canary group for more coverage.
Elaine: thanks. If numbers hold we'll ship a soft rollback + telemetry then plan a proper packing redesign.
Sam: agreed. Add postmortem note to the eng-runtime channel after we confirm stability.
Micah: Will do. Thanks all.
